CVE-2026-102960.title: Stack buffer overflow in Grow R502-A fingerprint sensor driver UART RX handler
CVE-2026-102960.description:
The Grow R502-A fingerprint sensor driver (drivers/sensor/grow_r502a/grow_r502a.c) receives sensor responses in the UART interrupt handler uart_cb_handler(). Once the 9-byte header has arrived, the handler reads the 16-bit package length from the header and uses it as the byte count for further uart_fifo_read() calls into rx_buf.data. It never checks that length against the destination buffer. That buffer is a union r502a_packet on the calling thread's stack, set up by transceive_packet(), and is only CONFIG_R502A_DATA_PKT_SIZE + 12 bytes long (140 bytes by default).

A malicious or counterfeit sensor module, or an attacker who tampers with the UART wiring, can reply to any driver command with a header that declares a length of up to 65535 bytes. The ISR then writes that many attacker-supplied bytes past the end of the stack buffer. The existing length check in r502a_validate_rx_packet() runs only after the data has been written, so it does not prevent the overflow. Every sensor…

CVE-2026-115559.title: imaplib STARTTLS serves plaintext bytes buffered before the handshake as if they came over TLS
CVE-2026-115559.description: IMAP4.starttls() wraps the socket in TLS but leaves self._readbuf, imaplib's own read-ahead buffer, untouched. Any plaintext bytes that arrived in the same recv() as the tagged OK to STARTTLS are returned by readline() after the handshake, so the client treats them as the first responses on the protected channel. A network attacker who cannot break TLS can append forged lines after the server's OK, let the handshake complete with the real server and a valid certificate, and have the client accept the forged CAPABILITY and the forged tagged completion of the next command. This is the STARTTLS command/response injection class of CVE-2011-0411.

CVE-2026-123828.title: Node.js is vulnerable to a heap buffer overflow in HTTP/2 session.altsvc() via a long origin
CVE-2026-123828.description: A one-byte heap buffer overflow in Node.js HTTP/2 Alt-Svc handling lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker corrupt process memory. When an application passes an attacker-controlled value such as a request's :authority header to Http2Session.altsvc(), the AltSvc implementation in src/node_http2.cc allocates a buffer sized to the origin length and then writes it with a null terminator, placing one byte past the end of the allocation. A single request carrying a long but syntactically valid :authority triggers the out-of-bounds write, which aborts the process and serves as a remote heap-corruption primitive. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.

From 5.14.3 until 7.4.7, Astro's /_image endpoint compared the requested local-image path with the build output directory without preserving case on case-sensitive filesystems. A sibling directory whose path differed from the output directory only by letter case could therefore pass the containment check, allowing an unauthenticated requester to read image files accepted by the image service from outside the output directory. Exploitation required on-demand rendering with the @astrojs/node adapter, a case-sensitive filesystem, and a preexisting case-variant sibling directory; ordinary traversal to unrelated paths was already rejected. This issue is fixed in Astro version 7.4.7.

CVE-2026-135254.title: MISP Cross-Site Request Forgery in Correlation Cache and Occurrence Regeneration
CVE-2026-135254.description:
MISP is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in its correlation management functionality.

The top-correlation cache regeneration and occurrence count regeneration actions were accessible via bodyless GET requests and were triggered from the admin interface using plain hyperlinks rather than POST forms. Because these state-changing operations did not require a POST method and were reachable through simple URL navigation, an attacker who can induce an authenticated administrator to visit a malicious page or click a crafted link can trigger these operations without the administrator's explicit consent.

Impact:
- Unintended triggering of resource-intensive correlation regeneration processes
- Potential disruption of correlation data processing and increased server load
- No direct data disclosure or corruption is evidenced

Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52

CVE-2026-136501.title: Positioned writes go to another user's table through name and case matching
CVE-2026-136501.description:
To build positioned updates and to describe columns, psqlODBC matches the names in a statement against the catalog. Where it matched differently from the server, it used another table or column:

- Table and schema names were compared case-insensitively in its column-information cache, so users could be taken for another user's "Users", and the driver then evaluated that table's column default to answer @@IDENTITY.
- In FROM ONLY t, ONLY was taken for the table name.
- Column names were compared case-insensitively, so with Parse=1 the type of another column could decide the size of the application's buffer, which a fetch then overflowed.
- In a database whose encoding is single-byte, such as LATIN1 or SQL_ASCII, the server folds the accented letters of an unquoted name by its own locale, while the driver folded only A-Z, so ÉTAT could be taken for another user's "État" instead of état.
- On systems other than Windows, in a Turkish or Azeri locale, an unquoted I was not folded to i,…

Description

the scheme, the host nor the port of the resolved target, and it is not governed by

robots.txt fetch at any address reachable from the fetcher worker, including loopback interfaces,
private ranges and cloud metadata endpoints. Every crawled URL triggers a robots.txt fetch on a cache

CVE-2026-99442.title: nvmem: core: Fix OOB read for bit offsets of more than one byte
CVE-2026-99442.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvmem: core: Fix OOB read for bit offsets of more than one byte

When the bit offset is BITS_PER_BYTE or larger the read position is
advanced by `bytes_offset`. This is not taken into account in the
per-byte read loop which still reads `cell->bytes` resulting in an out of
bounds read of `bytes_offset` bytes. The information read OOB does not
leak directly as the erroneously read bits are cleared.

Detected by KASAN while looking for a use-after-free in simplefb.c.

CVE-2026-99626.title: drm/amd/display: Fix NULL deref in dcn401_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto
CVE-2026-99626.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amd/display: Fix NULL deref in dcn401_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto

[Why]
resource_get_otg_master_for_stream() can return NULL if no OTG master pipe
is found for a given stream. The current code dereferences this pointer
without a NULL check. This may lead to a possible NULL pointer
dereference.

[How]
Add an explicit NULL check and skip the stream if the OTG master is not
found. This is similar to dcn60_update_clocks_update_dtb_dto().

Found by Linux Verification Center (linuxtesting.org) with SVACE.

CVE-2026-99653.title: mm: fix unkillable fault loop on MAP_DROPPABLE memory
CVE-2026-99653.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm: fix unkillable fault loop on MAP_DROPPABLE memory

handle_mm_fault() suppresses VM_FAULT_OOM for VM_DROPPABLE mappings.

For user-mode faults, pending signals are processed before retrying the
access. Kernel-mode faults on user buffers instead return directly to
the faulting instruction.

With persistent allocation failures (esp. memcg limits), a syscall,
such as write(), can therefore loop while not dropping locks.

Only suppress VM_FAULT_OOM when FAULT_FLAG_USER is set, allowing
kernel-mode faults and GUP to fail and signal allocation errors.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.
